stories.headline: U.N. committee calls for addressing ‘hate speech’ and ‘hate crimes’ in India
stories.deck: The committee calls on India to “urgently address discrimination, hate speech and hate crimes” and “ensure accountability” for these violations
stories.bodyText:
The official Indian delegation at the 11th periodic review of the State of India by the UN Committee on Elimination of Racial Discrimination (UNCERD) had “rejected” the findings of the Committee, said official sources on Tuesday (August 26, 2026).
The remarks shared with The Hindu came hours after the UNCERD said that it was “gravely concerned” about the reports of violations of human rights of a vast segment of the people of India, including the scheduled tribes, scheduled castes, Dalits and Rohingya refugees.
In a press note that called for addressing “hate speech” and “hate crimes” in India, the Committee said that there has been an increase in incidents against the Bengali-speaking Muslims and called on the Government of India to “ensure accountability” for these violations.
“During the review, India highlighted constitutional safeguards, a robust legal framework, pluralism and sustained efforts to protect disadvantaged communities. The inter-Ministerial delegation, led by the Solicitor General of India, had already rejected the sweeping generalisations, unsubstantiated allegations, or tendency to exceed the Convention’s mandate during the review meeting,” said an official source in response to a question from The Hindu.
Earlier, the UNCERD had issued a press note and said, “The Committee was gravely concerned about reports of large-scale violations perpetrated by law enforcement officials against ethnic and ethno-religious groups, Indigenous and Tribal Peoples, including Scheduled Tribes, Scheduled Castes, particularly Dalits, and non-citizens.”
The Committee, in its remarks, also mentioned that these communities have been subjected to “racially motivated violence, excessive use of force, extrajudicial killings, arbitrary and prolonged detention without due process, torture, ill-treatment and sexual violence”. The Government of India had sent Solicitor General Tushar Mehta as the Head of the Indian Delegation for the review.
“The Committee called on India to conduct prompt, thorough and impartial investigations into all such allegations and ensure accountability for those responsible,” said a press note issued by the Committee that coincided with the ninth anniversary of the Rohingya refugee crisis.
The UN Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination further noted that there has been an increase in law enforcement operations targeting “Rohingya, Bengali-speaking Muslims, migrants and asylum-seekers, particularly following the 2017 Home Affairs order and the April 2025 Pahalgam attack in Kashmir”. It found that police check posts resorted to racial profiling that led to “arbitrary arrest and detention without due process”.
“The Committee called on India to urgently address discrimination, hate speech and hate crimes against Rohingya, Bengali-speaking Muslims, migrants and asylum-seekers, protect their rights, refrain from collective expulsions and ensure access to international protection in line with the principle of non-refoulement,” the news release from the Committee said.

stories.headline: Veteran filmmaker Kuku Kohli passes away
stories.bodyText: Mumbai: Veteran filmmaker Kuku Kohli passed away on Tuesday evening in Mumbai. He was 77.He is survived by his wife, actor Aruna Irani, and his two children from his first marriage to Rita Kohli — filmmakers Pooja Kohli and Karishma Kohli.Couple of days ago, Kohli was admitted to Kokilaben Dhirubhai Ambani Hospital after feeling unwell..'Mahabharat' actor Aasha Singh passes away in Mumbai; son pays emotional tribute.He passed away on Thursday evening.Kohli introduced Ajay Devgn to the film industry with Phool Aur Kaante, Kohli went on to direct films including Kohraam (1991), Suhaag (1994), Haqeeqat (1995), Anari No. 1, Zulmi, Yeh Dil Aashiqanaa and Woh Tera Naam Tha.He also gave Rohit Shetty his early experience as an assistant.

stories.headline: Suvendu vows to keep Mamata off the streets, TMC chairperson says not taking political sanyas
stories.deck: Over the past few years, the politics in West Bengal has hinged on the electoral contest between Suvendu Adhikari and Mamata Banerjee
stories.bodyText:
Referring to former Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee interacting with her supporters through social media, West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Monday (August 24, 2026) suggested that his predecessor remains active on Facebook and said that he will ensure that she does not hit the streets.
“Remain active on facebook. You will not have to go out on the streets anymore. I will also make arrangements so that you cannot go out on the streets,” the Chief Minister said, while addressing a press conference at the State Secretariat.
ALSO WATCH TMC in crisis: Mamta Banerjee’s leadership questioned as MLAs break away | The Hindu explains
Ms. Banerjee, who only a few hours ago reiterated that she will not be pushed into a political sanyas, described the remark as a threat.
“A NEW LOW in Indian politics! @SuvenduWB, while seated in a government office, has brazenly THREATENED me, publicly declaring that he will ensure I cannot even leave my home. I call upon the Hon’ble President of India, the Hon’ble Chief Justice of India, and the people of India: Is this the India envisioned by our Constitution?” the Trinamool Congress chairperson wrote on X in a late evening post. A number of leaders of the Trinamool Congress joined Ms. Banerjee in taking on the Chief Minister.
After the defeat in the West Bengal Assembly polls 2026, Ms. Banerjee, who made her political mark as a ‘street-fighter ’, has not hit the streets often. On a few occasions she tried to do so the response has been tepid.
Mr. Adhikari cited the two instances of Baruipur, where a minor was raped and killed, and Halisahar, where a Trinamool supporter was killed in police custody and said that she failed at both the occasions.
However, the remark to keep the Trinamool Congress chairperson confined to social media has larger ramifications. Despite her party facing the biggest existential crisis – with majority of MPs and MLAs switching sides and warming up to the BJP, Mamata Banerjee remains the only leader to take on the might of the BJP which has 207 MLAs in a 294 member house.
Over the past few years, the politics in West Bengal has been hinged on a contest between an ageing leader who wants to pass over the baton to her nephew and one of her closest aides turned rival. Suvendu Adhikari has defeated Mamata Banerjee directly in an electoral contest on two occasions — in Nandigram in the 2021 Assembly polls by a margin of 1956 votes and in 2026 at Bhabanipur by a margin of 15,065 votes. The 2026 Assembly polls might not be the end of political rivalry, and people of West Bengal may continue to see the two political personalities taking on each other.
There is an enthusiasm among the BJP leadership after coming to power, but the Suvendu Adhikari government is caught in the same policy trap of giving cash doles which had been a hallmark of the Trinamool Congress regime.
With women protesting the denial of cash incentives under Annapurna Bhandar scheme as promised by the BJP during the election campaign, Mamata Banerjee sees it as an opportunity to revive both her credibility and her party.
There is also unease among the leaders who left Mamata Banerjee to warm up to the BJP, particularly those who are from the minority community, and that can be a silver lining for the Trinamool Congress chairperson. For Suvendu Adhikari, the challenge is how long can they keep the former Chief Minister confined to her residence and social media.

stories.headline: Post-Covid, profits rise faster than investment
stories.deck: One explanation identified by the study is that strong profitability from assets companies already own does not necessarily make a new investment equally attractive. Its analysis found evidence that the initial returns associated with fresh fixed-asset investment have weakened in the post-pandemic period, putting downward pressure on what the paper calls “marginal profitability”.
stories.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Corporate profits have recovered much faster than investment after the pandemic, with aggregate profit before interest and tax (PBIT) growing 21.4% in FY24 against 6.1% growth in gross fixed assets (GFA), an Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister working paper has found.
Profitability itself has risen too. Median return on assets (ROA) in the study sample increased from 4.4% in FY21 to 7.2% in FY24.
The contrast is therefore not between rising profits and falling investment. Corporate investment has also recovered after Covid, but at a considerably slower and less sustained pace. Gross fixed asset growth, which the paper uses as a proxy for fixed-asset investment, moved from a contraction of 1.1% in FY21 to growth of 2.2% in FY22, 6.8% in FY23 and 6.1% in FY24. Over the same three post-pandemic recovery years, PBIT grew 15.2%, 12.8% and 21.4%.
One explanation identified by the study is that strong profitability from assets companies already own does not necessarily make a new investment equally attractive. Its analysis found evidence that the initial returns associated with fresh fixed-asset investment have weakened in the post-pandemic period, putting downward pressure on what the paper calls “marginal profitability”.
Median return on assets (ROA) in the study sample increased from 4.4% in FY21 to 7.2% in FY24.
In other words, a company can be earning strongly from its existing plant and machinery but still hold back on adding another plant if it expects the additional investment to deliver lower returns.
The paper said global economic uncertainty, trade imbalances and the possibility of rapid technological change making existing technologies obsolete could also be weighing on investment decisions, although it did not separately test the impact of demand or uncertainty. It found no evidence that greater market concentration or financial constraints were important explanations for the gap between profitability and investment. Nor did it find a broad shift of companies towards asset-light business models.
Instead, manufacturing companies appear to be generating more revenue from their existing fixed assets, pointing to improved capacity utilisation. The paper said this was a positive development that could eventually create conditions for another round of investment.
Investment recovery also differed by ownership. Foreign-owned firms showed a continuing decline in weighted average investment intensity after the FY20 peak, while the recovery among Indian private firms levelled off after an initial improvement. Companies belonging to Indian business groups showed a more sustained recovery.
The paper also found that the investment peak in FY20 was partly driven by unusually high investment intensity among some large, asset-rich companies. Such an outlier spike disappeared during the pandemic and had not returned by FY24, helping explain why the subsequent investment recovery has been more muted. The study used CMIE Prowess financial data for 48,896 companies, including 5,614 listed and 43,282 unlisted firms.

 FY25 data was excluded from most of the quantitative analysis because corporate filings and the database for the year were largely incomplete.
Based on its findings, the paper recommended continuing and intensifying production-linked incentive schemes and public infrastructure investment aimed at crowding in private investment. It also called for greater support for innovative firms, stronger links between industry and academia, and faster contract enforcement and commercial dispute resolution.

briefs.bodyText: Bengaluru: The Department of Skill and Entrepreneurship has organised a ‘Study Abroad ‘ Expo in Bengaluru on September 6 for students aspiring to travel overseas for higher education..Medical Education and Skill Development Minister Dr Sharan Prakash Patil told a press meet here on Tuesday that over 60 foreign universities have confirmed their participation and 75 have shown interest to take part. briefs.headline: Karnataka: Heavy rains return to parts of Malnad region
briefs.deck: Heavy rains return to parts of Malnad region
briefs.bodyText: Bengaluru: Heavy rains returned to parts of Malnad region on Tuesday resulting in overflowing of streams and triggering landslides in parts of Dakshina Kannada and Kodagu districts. No human casualties were reported across the state..The monsoon rains, which picked up pace since Monday evening, returned to Karnataka shores after nearly a 20-day break. IMD has issued Yellow alert for Dakshina Kannada, Udupi, Kodagu and Mysuru for August 26..The Triveni Sangama at Bhagamandala (near the birthplace of River Cauvery) submerged on Tuesday..Kodagu district’s Sampaje (144 mm) received the highest rainfall followed by Galibidu (129 mm) and Peraje (112 mm)..Karnataka: Heavy rain lashes Subrahmanya, water levels in rivers rise.Heavy rains lashed parts of Dakshina Kannada also with temple town of Kukke Subrahmanya witnessing showers from Tuesday morning, causing the water level in the Kumaradhara and Darpana Theertha rivers near Adi Subrahmanya to rise significantly..Inflow to Hidkal dam also increased following copious rainfall in catchment areas of Ghataprabha and Hiranyakeshi in Western Ghats of Maharashtra.

briefs.headline: Pune tribal students’ protest enters 13th day as talks with Tribal Minister yield no breakthrough, say students
briefs.deck: Vijay Waghmare, a Secretary in the Tribal Department, said that the Ministry has issued a stay order on the major demand of the students, that is, regarding the Government Resolution (GR) issued on August 14, 2026
briefs.bodyText:
The students’ protest at a government tribal boys’ hostel in Pune continued for the 13th day on Tuesday (August 25, 2026), a day after ten students met Tribal Minister Dr. Ashok Ramaji Uike at Mantralaya in Mumbai but failed to secure assurances on their demands.
Vijay Waghmare, a Secretary in the Tribal Department, said that the Ministry has issued a stay order on the major demand of the students, that is, regarding the Government Resolution (GR) issued on August 14, 2026. “The government has met the major demand of the students regarding the Hostel Admissions GR. We have continued to interact with them and responded positively to their other demands. However, it will take time for putting them into action,” he said.
According to Balakrishna Gawari, a member of the Students Federation of India (SFI), the discussions ended without any significant progress or agreement on their demands, and they were asked to continue their protests. “They told us that they could not give us a definite written agreement to their demands, and that we could continue the protests if we wanted to,” he said.
Mr. Gawari also said that the students sought action over an alleged 12,500 government posts reserved for Scheduled Tribes that had been occupied by non-tribal candidates using fake caste certificates. “Those posts should be made vacant and should be filled with deserving people who belong to the Scheduled Tribe, and action should be taken against fake adivasis,” Mr. Gawari said.
Sharad Thokal, 26; Vijay Bhandble, 25; Rahul Dhanwe, 26; and Rajaram Padvi, 20, are continuing their hunger strike at the Adivasi Government Boys Hostel near the Hadapsar-Manjari border. Shweta Girnak, 26; Nikita Mechkar, 22 were admitted to the hospital on Monday evening due to poor health.
Some important demands the tribal students are seeking are that allowances and other financial provisions be linked to the Consumer Price Index so that they increase annually in line with inflation. increased protection for students staying in tribal hostels and ashram schools, and an insurance cover of ₹10 crore for every tribal student. This follows the recent deaths of three tribal students in a snakebite incident in Gadchiroli. The students have also sought compensation of ₹1 crore each for the families.
Other key demands include a safe and well-equipped central hostel building for female students in Pune and the immediate filling of vacant posts in hostels and ashram schools, including posts for peons, security guards, and sanitation workers, either permanently or on a contractual basis until regular recruitment is completed.

briefs.headline: Pained over wasted House time, says Legislative Council chairman Saleem Ahmed
briefs.deck: Pained over wasted House time, says Saleem Ahmed
briefs.bodyText: Bengaluru: Legislative Council Chairman Saleem Ahmed on Tuesday said he was “pained” to see precious House time lost to protests over eight days, but remained optimistic that the next session would be conducted smoothly, with members exercising restraint and participating in debates..Addressing a press briefing after the prolonged deadlock in both Houses of Karnataka Legislature forcing their adjournment sine die, Ahmed said the Opposition had adopted a single-point agenda of demanding the resignation of Planning and Statistics minister B Nagendra, refusing to give notice or a reasoned explanation for the demand..“I have served as a member of the Upper House for more than 16 years. There used to be debates and protests, but this is the first time the Opposition has remained adamant and disrupted the House with a single-point agenda,” he said..Karnataka | The monsoon legislature session that was...or wasn’t.Stating that the Opposition members tapping desks and raising slogans for nearly 20 hours was unprecedented. “What did they achieve by protesting for eight days? I was duty-bound to conduct the House, though it has pained me,” he said..Ahmed said he repeatedly asked the BJP-JDS leaders to give notice so the issue could be taken up as per the rules, but they insisted that the minister resign or they would not allow the House to function. Even Chief Minister D K Shivakumar had urged them to give notice on the second day, he said..The Chairman said the deadlock continued despite appeals in the Business Advisory Committee to facilitate discussions on crucial issues, including drought. He said he was particularly pained to see Bills being passed without debate as the Opposition chose not to participate. He also objected to the language used during the protests and the bringing of placards into the House..“I am pained that the House was chaotic when schoolchildren were watching the proceedings from the visitors’ gallery,” he said, adding that the conduct of the members was not good for democracy..The 159th session of the Legislative Council transacted business for 25 hours and 30 minutes in eight days, received 1,210 questions, including 120 starred and 1,090 unstarred, while 16 Assembly-passed Bills received the Council’s concurrence.

briefs.bodyText: Bengaluru: Following a six-day protest inside the Legislature, the BJP on Tuesday announced a 10-day padayatra from Raichur to Ballari to protest the ‘failures’ of the Congress government..Addressing a press conference, Karnataka BJP president B Y Vijayendra said: “The chief minister is not interested in development, farmers’ problems, lack of jobs, problems in implementing reservation, issues of North Karnataka, new recruitment and so on. To expose the Congress in front of the people of the state, we are taking out a padayatra.”.Stating that the 10-day Padayatra from September 1 through 10 would be held from Raichur to Ballari covering 200 km on average, Vijayendra said that Union Ministers would be in attendance at the valedictory event in Ballari. “This is a padayatra by the BJP. briefs.headline: Karnataka gives food business operators 15 days to set right safety deficiencies
briefs.deck: State gives food biz operators 15 days to set right safety deficiencies
briefs.bodyText: Bengaluru: Karnataka has given Food Business Operators (FBOs) 15 days to rectify deficiencies related to food safety, cleanliness and hygiene found during a recently conducted special inspection drive..In an advisory, the Food Safety and Drug Administration Department (FDA) has directed the operators to ensure they possess valid FSSAI licences or registrations and comply with all applicable food safety regulations. They have also been told to use only safe and wholesome food and immediately segregate and dispose of expired, spoiled or contaminated food products..The advisory also laid down requirements for maintaining kitchens and premises, properly cleaning and sanitising food-contact surfaces and equipment, preventing pest infestation and maintaining prescribed temperatures for perishable items such as milk, meat, eggs and prepared food. Refrigerators, freezers and other temperature control equipment must also be kept in working condition..Food safety violations detected in prominent clubs of Bengaluru.Food handlers have been directed to maintain personal hygiene, wear clean protective clothing and wash their hands frequently and properly while handling food. The advisory also stresses the use of safe water and ice, proper labelling of packaged foods and appropriate disposal of food waste..Food handlers should also receive necessary food-safety training and undergo health examinations as required..The operators have been directed to cooperate with Food Safety Officers during inspections and rectify any deficiencies within the stipulated period..After 15 days, the Food Safety Officers concerned will conduct re-inspections. If the deficiencies remain unrectified or violations continue, legal action will be initiated under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and the rules and regulations made under it, according to the department.

briefs.headline: Green gram yield to come a cropper in north Karnataka this year
briefs.deck: Green gram yield to come a cropper in north K'taka this yr
briefs.bodyText: Dharwad: As the harvest of green gram starts, the yield is expected to decline by around 30%, with the crop facing a combination of rainfall deficit, disease and lower sowing..A 35% rainfall deficit, compounded by yellow mosaic disease triggered by prolonged cloudy weather, has hit the crop..Apart from this, excessive vegetative growth, delayed pod formation, pest attacks and falling market prices have pushed growers across seven districts of North Karnataka into a difficult situation this season..Rain deficit hits 175 Karnataka taluks; 14 face severe shortage.Delays in opening government procurement centres have added to their woes..The crop was sown in 87% of its target area of 4.5 lakh hectares in the state this kharif season..Green gram is an important short-duration cash crop in Dharwad, Gadag, parts of Haveri, Koppal, Belagavi, Bagalkot and Vijayapura and also Yadgir — collectively regarded as Karnataka’s green gram belt. Agriculture scientists and farmers expect yields to decline by 25-30% due to erratic weather, pest and disease attacks..Other pulse and oilseed crops, including black gram, soybean and groundnut, have also come under stress because of unpredictable weather, increasing their vulnerability to pests and diseases..Together, these districts account for nearly half of Karnataka’s total green gram acreage of 3.99 lakh hectares and contribute over 60% of the state’s production..However, delayed monsoon and other weather-related factors have brought down the area under green gram this season to less than two lakh hectares in these districts, say farmers and agriculture officials..The early onset of the southwest monsoon encouraged farmers to complete sowing ahead of schedule. However, June remained largely dry, exposing the crop to severe moisture stress..Above-normal rainfall in July and prolonged drizzle and cloudy weather that followed created conditions conducive to what experts describe as “green drought”, while accelerating the spread of pests and viral diseases..Dr B H Prasannakumar, assistant professor of agronomy at University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS), Dharwad, said prolonged dry spell had severely affected green gram and black gram cultivation..“The major pulse-growing taluks have suffered the greatest damage, and yields are likely to decline by nearly 25%. While some taluks received good rainfall, yellow mosaic disease has severely affected the crops,” he told DH..He said yellow mosaic disease is transmitted by whiteflies, which rapidly spread the virus from one plant to another..Manjunath Antaravalli, joint director of agriculture, Dharwad said pest attacks had been reported in green gram, black gram and soybean fields and that the department had intensified awareness programmes to guide farmers on timely control measures..Farmer Mallikarjun Balangoudar said the lush green appearance of the fields was misleading..Kolar: Crop loss survey report submitted to state government.“The crops look healthy, but they are actually under severe moisture stress. Pod formation has been poor and yields will be much lower this season,” he said..He said the cost of cultivation had risen to nearly Rs 8,000 per hectare, while returns were expected to be poor..“Normally, we harvest around 500 kg per hectare, but this year we may get only 300 kg,” he said..With green gram now arriving in the market, farmers are facing another setback — prices below minimum support price (MSP)..Farmer Rajshekar Doddmani of Bagalkot said the government had fixed the MSP for green gram at Rs 8,780 per quintal, but the crop was fetching only around Rs 7,500 per quintal in open market..“The government has so far not opened procurement centres to purchase the produce. Farmers need money urgently to prepare for rabi sowing and cannot afford to hold on to their stocks. But selling at prevailing market price means incurring loss,” he said..“Due to drought, yield has declined by 25-30%, and now prices are also lower in the open market. The government should intervene and open procurement centres to purchase the harvest,” said Shankar Hiremath, another farmer.

briefs.headline: Iran, Oman hold talks on managing Strait of Hormuz
briefs.deck: A joint statement by the two countries said the proposed framework includes a “joint temporary navigational corridor” and both countries working to clear mines from the waterway
briefs.bodyText:
Omani Foreign Minister Badr al-Busaid met Tuesday (August 25, 2026) with his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi in Tehran to discuss a framework for managing ship traffic in the Strait of Hormuz.
A joint statement by the two countries, located on opposite sides of the narrow strait, said the proposed framework includes a “joint temporary navigational corridor” and both countries working to clear mines from the waterway.
The statement said Iran and Oman will continue technical negotiations toward establishing a permanent shipping corridor and an agreement on the future administration of the strait.
About a fifth of the world's traded oil passed through the strait before the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran on Feb 28.
It's unknown whether the U.S. will accept the emerging deal. U.S. President Donald Trump last week threatened to bomb Oman if it “gets in the way” of American efforts to reopen the strait.

stories.headline: Why Urvashi was Bengaluru’s best single screen
stories.deck: Urvashi Cinema, one of Bengaluru’s most iconic single-screen theatres, is set to close its doors after 50 years.
stories.bodyText:
Urvashi Cinema, one of Bengaluru’s most iconic single-screen theatres, is set to close its doors after 50 years. For generations of filmgoers, it was more than just a theatre — it was a place where first-day-first-shows, fan celebrations, whistles, cheers and countless movie memories came alive. Urvashi has screened several blockbusters of ShahRukhKhan, Yash and Rajinikanth.
It was once a go-to-place for big Hollywood movies. As Bengaluru continues to change, the closure of Urvashi marks the end of another chapter in the city’s rich single-screen culture. This is a small tribute to a theatre that remained a favourite among movie lovers since 1976.

stories.headline: After 540 days of protests, Karnataka CM invites those opposing Bidadi Township for talks
stories.deck: The move came after farmers brought their protest to Bengaluru’s Freedom Park and announced that they would lay siege to Vidhana Soudha
stories.bodyText:
After 540 days of protests against the Bidadi Township, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Tuesday (August 25, 2026) finally invited farmers opposing the project for talks and assured them that no land would be acquired forcefully.
The delegation that met the Chief Minister told The Hindu that Mr. Shivakumar had assured them that the government would not proceed with steps following the final notification, including fixing the final price.
Yashavantha T., State General Secretary of the Karnataka Prantha Raitha Sangha (KPRS), said Mr. Shivakumar had stated that the government would proceed with the project based on the report of the committee headed by Justice (Retd.) Guhanathan Narendar, former Chief Justice of the Uttarakhand High Court, which has been appointed to re-examine the project from various perspectives.
One of the demands placed before the delegation was the inclusion of more experts from environmental, social and agricultural sectors in the committee. Mr. Shivakumar agreed to the demand, Mr. Yashavantha said. He added that they would submit the names of the experts from their side within two days. The final report of the committee is expected to be submitted in 20 days.
“Regarding denotification, the Chief Minister said that he can’t do it, but once the time lapses, farmers can move the court and get their lands denotified. The petitions won’t be challenged,” Mr. Yashavantha said.
M.R. Nagaraju, a farmer from Mandalahalli who has been at the forefront of the protest, told The Hindu that opposition to the project would continue at Bairamangala Circle, but with less intensity. “We will wait for the committee report to come out, after which we will decide on calling off the protests,” he said.
Protest called off
The talks initiated by Mr. Shivakumar came after farmers, who had been protesting at Bairamangala Circle for over 540 days, brought their protest to Bengaluru’s Freedom Park and announced that they would lay siege to Vidhana Soudha on Tuesday.
Before they could stage a rally, several farmer leaders, including Badagalapura Nagendra, Chukki Nanjundaswamy, Melukote MLA Darshan Puttannaiah, actor Prakash Raj, and several others, gathered at Freedom Park. Subsequently, a huge police deployment was also made.
However, even before the rally could commence, the Chief Minister’s Office contacted the leaders and invited them for a discussion. briefs.headline: SIR in Karnataka: Chief Minister seeks more time for SIR claims, verification
briefs.deck: ‘Mobility should not translate into disenfranchisement,’ Shivakumar said in his letter to the ECI
briefs.bodyText:
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar has urged the Election Commission of India to extend the time available for submitting claims and objections and verification of voters during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Karnataka.
In a letter to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, Mr. Shivakumar said the scale of names placed under the Absent, Shifted, Dead, Duplicate and Others (ASDDO) categories and those facing verification over “logical discrepancies” warranted adequate time and a proper verification process.
According to the letter, nearly 1.08 crore of Karnataka’s 5.54 crore electors have been placed in the ASDDO category. Following publication of the draft rolls on August 24, around 43.8 lakh electors are expected to receive notices over “logical discrepancies” or the absence of a link to the 2002 electoral roll.
‘Mobility should not mean disenfranchisement’
Mr. Shivakumar said a significant number of voters categorised as “Absent” could be genuine electors who were away from home when Booth Level Officers (BLOs) visited them, including for work, health or other reasons.
Similarly, voters who had shifted to another polling station were not given an opportunity to submit enumeration forms at their new addresses during the house-to-house exercise, he said.
“In Bengaluru and other cities, even moving across the street can mean a change of polling station,” the Chief Minister said, pointing out that such voters would now have to file Form 6 for inclusion in the rolls.
He expressed concern that voters categorised as Absent or Shifted would not receive the notices being issued to those facing “logical discrepancies” and “unmapped” status, and could therefore remain unaware that their names had been deleted.
“Mobility should not translate into disenfranchisement,” Mr. Shivakumar said.
Longer verification period
The Chief Minister sought an extension of the claims and objections period so that voters whose names are missing from the draft rolls, including those in the ASDDO categories, have sufficient time to ascertain their status and file claims.
He referred to the 2023 Manual of Electoral Roll and said the prescribed period could be extended by the Election Commission through a notification.
Mr. Shivakumar also sought a minimum of three to four weeks for voters facing verification over “logical discrepancies” or lack of a link to the 2002 roll to respond and produce documents.
He said the proposed process, involving notices and disposal of cases within about 45 days, could put an unreasonable burden on working people, migrants and the elderly, particularly when documents need to be obtained or voters have to travel.
Ward meetings, Gram Sabhas sought
The Chief Minister also urged the CEO to specifically direct District Election Officers to convene Ward Committee meetings in urban areas and Gram Sabhas in rural areas, with adequate advance publicity.
He said the draft rolls should be read out at these meetings so that omissions and errors could be identified and corrected.
While referring to the CEO’s August 20 communication on the provision, Mr. Shivakumar said merely referring to the procedure without specifically directing the meetings could result in it becoming a “pro forma compliance” rather than an effective mechanism for detecting errors.
More officials sought
The Chief Minister also sought an increase in the number of Additional Electoral Registration Officers and District Election Officers in districts with a high number of ASDDO cases and “logical discrepancies”.
He said the large number of objections and applications expected during the claims process, combined with the limited time available, could place an enormous workload on the existing machinery.
The State government, he said, was ready to provide assistance, including mobilising local administration for Gram Sabha and Ward Committee meetings, undertaking publicity campaigns and providing logistical support.
“The objective must be an electoral roll that the people of Karnataka can trust,” he added.

briefs.deck: Among the Bills was the controversial Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which allows 5% of park land to be sold, leased, gifted, exchanged or mortgaged for public utility projects undertaken by government departments, statutory authorities, government companies or local bodies
briefs.bodyText:
Ten Bills were tabled and passed by the Karnataka Legislative Assembly and Council on Monday (August 24, 2026) without debate, as BJP and JD(S) members continued to protest inside and outside the House demanding the resignation of Minister B. Nagendra, who has been chargesheeted in the alleged embezzlement of funds in the Maharshi Valmiki Scheduled Tribes Development Corporation.
Among the Bills was the controversial Karnataka Government Parks (Preservation) (Amendment) Bill, 2026, which allows up to 5% of park land to be sold, leased, gifted, exchanged or mortgaged for public utility projects undertaken by government departments, statutory authorities, government companies or local bodies.
The amendment is largely aimed at facilitating infrastructure projects, including the proposed 17.1-km Bengaluru North-South Twin Tunnel Road, which will connect Hebbal with Central Silk Board Junction. If enacted, the law could potentially allow up to 5% of the land at Lalbagh Botanical Garden to be utilised for such projects.
The proposal has already drawn strong opposition from citizen groups, environmentalists and BJP MPs from Bengaluru.
Bills cleared
Land previously alienated
The Bill provides for an evaluation mechanism headed by the Additional Chief Secretary, along with designated officers and domain experts, to assess proposals for using park and garden land before making recommendations to the government.
It stipulates that the 5% ceiling will include land previously alienated, while routine development undertaken by the Horticulture Department for its own administrative and allied purposes will remain outside the restriction.
The amendment also provides a legal framework for using small portions of horticulture farms for projects such as post-processing facilities, cold-storage units, production of improved crop varieties and agro-based industries that benefit local farmers, subject to recorded reasons establishing public interest and necessity.
Earlier cases of use of park land
The Bill cites previous instances of park land being used for road widening and metro projects. These include 1,223 sq. metres of the Indira Gandhi Musical Fountain Park given to the erstwhile Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP) for road widening, and 1,135 sq. metres of Lalbagh Gardens, along with a portion of its western compound wall, transferred to the Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited for the construction of an elevated metro station on R.V. Road.

stories.headline: Madras built the engine, Chennai is shifting gears
stories.deck: From a colonial trading centre to a manufacturing hub and now a diversified global business destination, the city has repeatedly reinvented itself. Chennai is now home to leading global firms, building on the foundation laid by Madras
stories.bodyText:
Before Chennai became a city of multinational firms, Global Capability Centres, semiconductor ambitions, aerospace and defence majors, automobile giants, footwear factories, startups and home grown firms, it was Madras — a city whose business story was already taking shape several centuries ago. From a colonial trading centre to a manufacturing hub and now a diversified global business destination, the city has repeatedly reinvented itself.
Business really mattered to Madras. The industrial development of the Madras Presidency was a matter of serious concern and in 1899, a whole time officer (later Sir) Alfred Chatterton who was then with the College of Engineering, Guindy, was appointed to stimulate industrial technical education in the region, according to details documented in a coffee table book titled Championing Enterprise – 175 years of the Madras Chamber of Commerce and Industry. The government decided to create a department to survey existing industries and investigate the possibility of creating new ones, it said.
“Trade came first. From Fort St. George in 1639, Madras shipped rather than made — cotton piece goods, indigo, hides. The artificial harbour of the 1880s turned an open roadstead into a working port, and that decision still explains where our industry sits. Then factories. Binny’s Buckingham Mill in 1876 and the Carnatic Mill in 1881 employed tens of thousands at Perambur. Parry moved from trading into sugar and chemicals. Simpson began coach building in 1840,” said Deepak Jacob, Managing Director and CEO of Guidance the nodal agency instrumental in bringing investments into Tamil Nadu.
“Trade built the port. The port brought the mills. The mills and the PSUs built the engineering base. That base brought the automakers, and the automakers brought electronics. What we build now is not for the investor in front of us. It is for the one who arrives in 2045,” he added.
Long before Chennai became known as the Detroit of India, Madras was already laying the foundations for the automotive sector. The first car to arrive in Madras was in the early 1900s. Simpson’s, the city’s famed coach builders then, played a role in this. In 1948, Madras had become home to automotive pioneers such as Standard Motor Products of India and Ashok Leyland (Ashok Motors), while Enfield India began two-wheeler manufacturing in 1956. Today, Chennai is home to several leading automobile companies, including TVS Motor Company.
Chennai has also embraced the electric-vehicle revolution, with several companies entering the EV space and adding a new dimension to the city’s automotive story.
Tractors and Farm Equipment Ltd (TAFE), headquartered in Chennai, is another interesting chapter in the city’s business story. India’s second largest tractor manufacturer, TAFE is led by Mallika Srinivasan, one of the few prominent women business leaders in the city, who has significantly expanded the company through strategic acquisitions and expansions across geographies.
The Madras Rubber Factory, known as MRF, began its journey in Madras as a small toy-balloon manufacturer and went on to become one of India’s largest tyre makers. Business conglomerates such as Murugappa Group, Sanmar Group, India Cements were all headquartered in Madras and expanding their businesses. Banks, too, joined the race. Indian Bank began its journey in Madras in 1907, followed by Indian Overseas Bank (IOB) in 1937. “Madras built its banks before its factory base, which was part of why services took root here so easily later,” Mr. Jacob said.
In 1958, Madras opened the Guindy Industrial Estate, one of India’s first industrial estates alongside Delhi’s Okhla. And the first phase was inaugurated by Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru.
Then came the IT revolution and the multinationals. “While much of the growth was led by home-grown companies, the participation of multinationals was largely through joint ventures and other forms of partnerships. It was only in the post liberalisation era that multinationals made a beeline for Chennai,” Ramkumar Ramamoorthy, Partner, Catalincs and former CMD, Cognizant India.
“Some of the biggest names in global business such as Ford, Cognizant, St. Gobain, and Hyundai made Chennai their home. This was followed by a flurry of investments by companies from across the globe. Examples include Caterpillar, Standard Chartered, Grundfos, Danfoss, Yamaha, Renault-Nissan, IBM, Accenture, BMW, World Bank, and Cap Gemini,” he added.
In the last two decades, Chennai has added a new chapter to its business story — startups. Once known primarily for factories, automobiles, and manufacturing, the city is now know as the SaaS (Software as a Service) hub. Chennai now has 5,134 startups, according to StartupTN. The IIT-Madras ecosystem has created a new generation of entrepreneurs, while the IIT-Madras Research Park has become a hotbed for innovation, deep tech and ideas moving from the lab to the market.
IIT-Madras Incubation Cell (IITMIC) began in 2013, at a time when “deep tech” was not a popular word, its Chief Executive Officer Tamaswati Ghosh said. She narrated that in the early days they were questioned how startups were staying with them. The answer came in the form of companies such as Ather Energy, which, despite eventually moving to Karnataka, became one of the early poster boys of Chennai’s startup ecosystem. Uniphore showed that founders need not be from Chennai to build here; its founders adopted the city and built the company from here, she pointed out.
Then came Agnikul, putting Chennai on the map for space tech innovation. In the past decade, Chennai has attracted several Global Capability Centers (GCCs). According to estimates, the city has over 300 GCCs. Logistics firms like Hapag Lloyd and United Parcel Service have chosen Chennai.
The least discussed of the new sectors is animation, VFX, and gaming. Phantom FX, Basilic Fly, Knack Studios, and BOT VFX are already here, hiring on a diploma rather than a doctorate. The AVGC-XR Policy 2026 targets two lakh jobs by 2030.
Chennai in 2030
“With Chennai having emerged as the data science hub of India with prominent pure-play analytics companies such as Latentview, Tiger, Tredence, Fractal, Crayon Data, and MathCo establishing their operations in the city, I expect significant AI innovation to happen from the city at the intersection of multiple domains and data analytics,” Mr. Ramamoorthy said.
He then added that while existing industries will continue to grow and thrive, the biggest drivers of growth and employment will come from GCCs, NBFCs, electronics, defence manufacturing, renewable energy, tourism (including medical tourism), and from MSMEs and new-age startups in areas such as fintech, healthtech, deeptech, spacetech, among others. “We will see companies in these new age sectors make significant investments in R&D and intellectual property, which should augur well for the state in improving its per capita income,” he noted.
“The base stays. In 2030 Chennai is still an automotive, electronics, and services city, and GCCs remain its highest-wage employer. What changes is where Chennai sits in the value chain. Today the design decision, the IP and the margin often sit elsewhere while we do the making. Closing that gap is the work,” Mr. Jacob added. Madras laid the foundation and Chennai is building what comes next.

stories.headline: Infrastructure projects see cost overrun of ₹3.4 lakh cr: MoSPI
stories.deck: A total of 1,775 ongoing infrastructure projects across 17 Central Ministries/ Departments were monitored, and it was found that the total revised cost was ₹37,10,642 crore compared to their original cost of ₹33,70,138 crore
stories.bodyText:
Infrastructure projects worth more than ₹150 crore each recorded a cumulative cost overrun of around ₹3,40,504 crore, according to a monthly government report for July 2026.
A total of 1,775 ongoing infrastructure projects across 17 Central Ministries/ Departments were monitored, and it was found that the total revised cost was ₹37,10,642 crore compared to their original cost of ₹33,70,138 crore.
The report, however, did not specify the actual number of projects that faced cost overrun.
The cumulative expenditure incurred on these projects stands at ₹19.26 lakh crore, accounting for approximately 51.91% of the revised project cost, indicating steady progress in project implementation, a statement by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) said.
A significant proportion of projects are at advanced stages, with 675 projects (38%) achieving over 80% physical progress, while 305 (17%) have crossed 80% financial completion.
The data also reflects a balanced pipeline, with projects distributed across early and advanced stages of implementation.
The Transport & Logistics sector accounts for the highest number of ongoing projects (1,246 projects), with revised estimates of Rs 19.81 lakh crore underscoring priority to connectivity-driven infrastructure growth.
1,775 ongoing infrastructure projects include 735 Mega projects (project cost of ₹1,000 crore & above) with an original cost of ₹28.77 lakh crore, and 1,040 Major projects (project cost below ₹1,000 crore and up to ₹150 crore) amounting to ₹4.93 lakh crore.
Physical and financial progress broadly move in tandem, with a large number of projects clustered at the initial (0–20%) and advanced (81–100%) stages, indicating a pipeline of newly started projects alongside many nearing completion.
While physical progress exceeds financial progress in the 81–100% range, financial progress is relatively higher in the early stages, reflecting upfront expenditure patterns in project implementation.
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways accounts for the highest number of projects, with 993 projects (56%) and a share of the total revised project cost of ₹9.62 lakh crore (26%), highlighting its central role in national infrastructure development.
Ministry of Railways is implementing 190 projects (11%), with a total revised project cost of ₹6.38 lakh crore (17%).
Ministry of Coal accounts for implementing 121 projects (7%), with a total revised project cost of ₹2.22 lakh crore (6%).
The Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas, Ministry of Power, Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs, and the Department of Water Resources, River Development & GR are implementing 103, 98, 50, and 38 projects, with associated revised costs of ₹4.23 lakh crore, ₹6.08 lakh crore, ₹3.78 lakh crore, and ₹2.01 lakh crore, respectively.
The remaining 182 projects (10%), with a total revised cost of ₹2.78 lakh crore (8%), are distributed across various Ministries/Departments, including Higher Education, Civil Aviation, Steel, Telecommunications, Labour & Employment, Ports, Shipping & Waterways, Health & Family Welfare, Mines, DPIIT, and Sports.
Transport & Logistics remains the dominant sector, accounting for 53% of the total revised project cost (₹19.81 lakh crore) across 1,246 projects (70% of the total projects), underscoring the central role of Roads & Highways, Railways, Aviation, Urban Public Transport, Shipping, and Inland Waterways in economic integration and logistics efficiency.
The Energy sector follows, with 29% of the aggregated revised cost (₹10.66 lakh crore) across 205 projects, reflecting sustained emphasis on Oil & Gas infrastructure, electricity generation, transmission and distribution networks, and energy storage systems.
Communication infrastructure, with a project cost of ₹1.34 lakh crore (4%) across 31 projects, represents targeted interventions aimed at strengthening digital connectivity.
Water & Sanitation projects account for Rs 2.05 lakh crore (5%) across 53 projects, highlighting continued focus on essential urban services.
Social & Commercial infrastructure, comprising 91 projects with a revised project cost of ₹0.99 lakh crore (3%), reflects selective investments in education, healthcare, real estate, and tourism, hospitality and wellness.
Projects classified under ‘Others’, amounting to ₹2.26 lakh crore (6%) across 149 projects, indicate diversification across sectors such as coal, steel, metals, and mining.

briefs.headline: For global scale banks, EAC-PM seeks mergers
briefs.deck: Beyond consolidation, banks need to narrow the credit-deposit gap, mobilise stable low-cost deposits and curb concentration in high-risk unsecured retail loans while expanding credit to MSMEs, infrastructure and green investments. To measure efficiency, the study treated banks as institutions that use resources such as fixed assets, borrowed funds, operating expenses and employee costs to…
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: A report published by the PM Economic Advisory Council has called for further consolidation of banks to create a few large institutions of similar size without compromising competition, as reforms over the past decade have sharply improved banking efficiency and reduced bad loans.
According to the report, authored by Soumya Kanti Ghosh and Tapas Kumar Parida, reforms including the Asset Quality Review (AQR), insolvency laws and earlier bank consolidations have improved efficiency across the banking sector. The authors said India would need larger, globally competitive financial institutions to meet the economy’s expanding credit requirements as it seeks to become a developed nation by 2047. “In this context, India should make efforts to consolidate the banks in such a manner that a few big banks of equal size would be created, without compromising market competition in the industry,” the report said.
Beyond consolidation, banks need to narrow the credit-deposit gap, mobilise stable low-cost deposits and curb concentration in high-risk unsecured retail loans while expanding credit to MSMEs, infrastructure and green investments.
To measure efficiency, the study treated banks as institutions that use resources such as fixed assets, borrowed funds, operating expenses and employee costs to generate loans, deposits, investments and net profits.
The findings show a significant turnaround in banking efficiency over the 12-year period from FY15 to FY26. The mean technical efficiency of scheduled commercial banks fell from 91.3% in FY15 to 78% in FY20 as bad loans were recognised and the Covid pandemic hit, before recovering to 88.3% in FY26. Public sector banks led the recovery. Their average technical efficiency fell to 72.5% in FY20 but rose to 93.1% in FY26 after recapitalisation and digital upgrades.

briefs.bodyText:
TOKYO: Amid concerns over some certification requirements, commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal Tuesday said that BIS (Bureau of Indian Standards) and his ministry will work out a framework to support high-tech industries looking to 
make in India
 by exempting equipment used by them from some of the norms.

It’s a very logical step, given that companies that come to make high-quality semicon products are going to get high-quality products into the country. You are not going to compromise on quality even if it comes cheaper,” the minister said during a meeting with semiconductor and AI companies here.

briefs.headline: RBI turns net buyer of dollars in June
briefs.deck: The shift narrowed RBI’s cumulative net sales for the fiscal year to -$14.5 billion and reduced its outstanding forward short position to -$103.3 billion. In the currency futures market, purchases and sales were balanced at $2.9 billion each, leaving zero net outstanding futures. The dollar purchases came as resident Indians increased outward remittances under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme.
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: 
RBI
 turned a net purchaser of US dollars in June this year, buying $561 million in the spot and over-the-counter market after net sales of $6.1 billion in May and $3.6 billion in June 2025.
According to the central bank’s monthly bulletin, the June purchase was equivalent to about Rs 5,505 crore and marked a shift in its currency market operations even as demand for foreign exchange from residents increased.
In June, RBI announced a scheme that allowed commercial banks to offer higher yields on NRI deposits while transferring the underlying currency risk to RBI through a swap. The measure helped increase dollar inflows, allowing the central bank to absorb surplus foreign exchange and rebuild its reserves. In the OTC segment, gross dollar purchases rose to $30.9 billion in June against sales of $30.3 billion.
The shift narrowed RBI’s cumulative net sales for the fiscal year to -$14.5 billion and reduced its outstanding forward short position to -$103.3 billion. In the currency futures market, purchases and sales were balanced at $2.9 billion each, leaving zero net outstanding futures. The dollar purchases came as resident Indians increased outward remittances under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme.
Remittances rose 6.5% month-on-month to $2.5 billion in June, nearly 20% higher than a year earlier.

Jana was among the microfinance lenders that received a specialised banking licence in 2017. It began operations as a small finance bank in March and went public in Feb 2024.
In its clarification, Federal Bank said it evaluates opportunities for growth and expansion in the ordinary course of business. It said, “there is no material event/ information that requires disclosure under Regulation 30” of Sebi’s Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements regulations.
Jana Small Finance Bank, responding to a request for clarification from BSE and NSE, said it evaluates “all opportunities in the ordinary course of business, from time to time”.
It said that going ahead, it would continue to make disclosures required under Regulation 30.

briefs.headline: RBI flags price risks, 2nd time in August

briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: The 
Indian economy
 remains resilient despite external headwinds, but below-normal monsoon prospects, higher crude oil prices, geopolitical tensions and global trade uncertainty pose risks to growth and inflation, according to the State of the Economy article in RBI’s Aug bulletin.
The assessment also pointed to firm domestic demand, improving industrial activity and strong corporate profitability as supports for growth.
This is the second hawkish statement to come from the central bank. Earlier, the minutes of the monetary policy committee meeting revealed that MPC members saw possibility of a rate hike in future. “Domestic demand remained strong in July, supported by rural demand. Retail automobile sales accelerated, led by stronger tractor and two-wheeler sales... Urban demand also remained firm,” the article said. Vehicle and tractor sales were among the indicators pointing to sustained demand.
Industrial activity also remained supportive. PMI data showed that firms’ expectations for future output improved, pointing to a positive outlook for demand and new business opportunities. The economy, the article said, “continued to display strength notwithstanding these headwinds”, while retail inflation in Q1:2026-27 reflected limited pass-through of cost pressures and growth remained resilient.
Inflation, however, has begun to face pressure from food prices. Headline CPI inflation increased marginally in July, driven by food and beverages. “High-frequency data suggest a broad-based sequential increase in food prices,” with rice and wheat prices continuing to rise, prices of major pulses edging up and edible oil prices recording broad-based increases. While headline inflation rose fractionally, core inflation remained stable. The article said the increase in headline inflation was primarily due to supply-side pressures and that stable core inflation indicated limited pass-through of cost pressures.
The IMD has forecast below-normal rainfall for the second half of the season in August and September. A weak monsoon could affect agricultural output and add to food inflation pressures.
Input costs also remain elevated. “Industrial and farm input cost inflation moderated, but remained elevated,” the article said.

briefs.headline: Tata Steel gets interim relief in ₹1,755 crore demand notice issued by Jharkhand government

briefs.bodyText:
Tata Steel has received interim relief in the ₹1,755-crore demand notice issued by the Jharkhand government, according to a regulatory filing.
The company has challenged a ₹1,755 crore mining demand notice issued by the District Mining Office, Ramgarh, Jharkhand, over alleged excess coal extraction of 16.24 million tonnes at the West Bokaro Colliery, beyond permissible limits, during 2000-01 to 2006-07.
The company was of the view that the demand lacked justification and substantive basis and had merit to challenge the demand. Accordingly, in April, Tata Steel had filed a Revision Application before the revisional authority of the coal ministry, challenging the demand notice.
The Revisional Authority heard the revision application.
The company hereby informs that the Revisional Authority has inter alia, passed the following directions – the Revision Application filed by Tata Steel Ltd has been admitted for consideration. The respondents are directed not to take any coercive steps against the Applicant pursuant to the impugned demand notices/letters, during the pendency of the present Revision Application," Tata Steel said in the filing.
Tata Steel will invest ₹11,000 crore in Jharkhand to develop advanced-grade steel at its Jamshedpur facility, Tata Group Chairman N Chandrasekaran had earlier said.
The technology developed by the Tata Group for advanced steel production will benefit other steelmakers, too, he had said.

briefs.headline: AMI orders 9,000 NVIDIA Rubin GPUs for Hyderabad facility
briefs.deck: The facility is expected to be among Asia’s first frontier AI computing clusters using the Vera Rubin platform, the company said in a press release
briefs.bodyText:
AM Intelligence, an infrastructure platform set up by Greenko promoters, on Tuesday (August 25, 2026) placed a binding order for 9,000 NVIDIA Rubin GPUs for what it described as its first AI factory here.
The order covers 9,000 NVIDIA Rubin GPUs to be deployed as Vera Rubin NVL72 systems at AMI’s 30 MW facility in Hyderabad in the first quarter of 2027.
The facility is expected to be among Asia’s first frontier AI computing clusters using the Vera Rubin platform, the company said in a press release.
The Hyderabad facility will be the first tranche of AMI’s planned 1 GW of Compute-as-a-Service capacity across India, the United States, Finland and Malaysia, it said.
AMI plans to bring 200 MW of capacity to market in the near term, involving capital expenditure of more than USD 8 billion, it added.
AMI chairman Anil Chalamalasetty said, "For over two decades, we have focused on transforming electrons into value — addressing critical and emerging societal needs. Today, the electron-to-token opportunity allows us to take this capability further, converting power infrastructure into frontier AI compute at scale." "Bringing the latest-generation NVIDIA Vera Rubin to India marks the next step in this journey and establishes AMI at the forefront of the emerging AI electron-to-token economy," he added.
AMI is developing 5 GW of powered AI data centres across India, the U.S. and Europe, integrating energy and next-generation computing to serve hyperscalers, sovereign AI initiatives, frontier labs and AI-native companies, the release said.
The facilities are being designed for high-density AI computing and will use liquid cooling to manage the substantial power and heat generated by advanced AI chips.
They will also be capable of accommodating successive generations of AI silicon, the release added.

briefs.headline: NASSCOM strongly responds to DHS’ proposal to fix H-1B visa fee at $103,265
briefs.deck: NASSCOM reminds the U.S administration that the number of H-1B employees Indian technology companies has reduced significantly as they steadily expanded local hiring. Also, Indian tech industry spent over $ 1.1 bn for strengthening STEM pipeline in the US working with over 130 universities and colleges impacting 2.9 million students and upskilling more than 255,000 employees
briefs.bodyText:
Strongly responding to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS)’s proposal to fix the H-1B visa fee at $103,265 for new applicants, the technology industry body NASSCOM on Tuesday (August 25, 2026) emphasised that the H-1B visa programme has long served an important purpose in addressing short-term skill gaps in the U.S.
The new $103,265 H-1B executive rule was a proposed U.S. Department of Homeland Security regulation in which the public has 30 days to comment, and according to the U.S administration, the fee would recover immigration-system costs and encourage employers to hire and train American workers instead of relying on foreign labour, NASSCOM stated.
However, the apex body also said, “It is also important to recognise that, over the past 5 years, the number of H-1B employees of Indian technology companies operating has reduced significantly, as companies have steadily expanded local hiring.’’
NASSCOM further maintained that the industry has also spent more than $1.1 billion on strengthening the STEM (science, technology, engineering and mathematics) pipeline in the U.S., working with more than 130 universities and colleges in the US impacting 2.9 million students and upskilling more than 255,000 employees.
“A proposed increase in visa fees must therefore be viewed in the context of the programme’s original purpose of enabling access to temporary skills where there is a shortage in the U.S.,’’ NASSCOM reminded the administration while promising that the industry body would remain actively engaged with all key stakeholders on this matter.

stories.headline: Bruno Fernandes crowned PFA Player of the Year to seal stunning awards hat-trick
stories.deck: Bruno Fernandes has completed a clean sweep of major individual awards after being named PFA Players’ Player of the Year for his outstanding 2025-26 season. The Manchester United captain broke the Premier League assist record with 21, scored nine goals and helped United finish third. He is the club’s first PFA Players’ Player winner since Wayne Rooney in 2010.
stories.bodyText:
Bruno Fernandes has capped a remarkable 2025-26 campaign by being named the PFA Players' Player of the Year, completing a personal clean sweep of the major individual awards after a season in which he rewrote the Premier League's assist record.
The 
Manchester United
 captain was recognised by his fellow professionals at the PFA Awards in Manchester on Tuesday evening, becoming the first United player to win the prestigious prize since Wayne Rooney in 2010.
Fernandes' victory came after he had already been named the Premier League Player of the Season and Football Writers' Association Footballer of the Year, meaning the Portugal international has now collected all three major individual honours available to him for his extraordinary campaign.
His 2025-26 season was defined by creativity as much as goals. Fernandes finished with 21 Premier League assists, breaking a record previously shared by Thierry Henry and Kevin De Bruyne, while also scoring nine goals as United secured third place and a return to the Champions League under manager Michael Carrick.
But his dominance was not confined to the individual award.
Fernandes was also selected in the PFA Premier League Team of the Year, where he was one of only two players from outside Arsenal and Manchester City to make the XI. 
The other was Brentford striker Igor Thiago.
Fernandes completes the individual-award hat-trick
Fernandes' PFA triumph is the latest recognition of a season in which he consistently stood out despite United's struggles in previous campaigns.
His record-breaking assist tally reached 21 on the final day of the Premier League season, when he provided the delivery for Patrick Dorgu's header against Brighton.
That moved him beyond the previous joint record of 20 assists held by Henry and De Bruyne and gave Fernandes the outright Premier League record for assists in a single season.
He finished the campaign with nine goals as United climbed to third in the table, securing Champions League qualification.
FILE - Manchester United's Bruno Fernandes walks off the pitch after the Premier League soccer match between Manchester United and Leeds in Manchester, England, April 13, 2026. (AP Photo/Dave Thompson, File)
The PFA award carries a particular significance because it is voted for by fellow professional footballers.
Fernandes, who attended Tuesday night's ceremony with his wife Ana, admitted that receiving recognition from players he competes against made the achievement particularly meaningful.
“It is obviously a very proud moment,” Fernandes said. “They are the ones you go on the pitch against and it's probably not easy to vote for someone you play against, so it is a very good moment.”
His win also restored United's presence at the top of the PFA's individual awards after a 16-year wait. Rooney was the last Manchester United player to win the men's Players' Player of the Year award, taking the honour for the 2009-10 season.
Fernandes has also become the first Portuguese Manchester United player to win the award since Cristiano Ronaldo, who claimed the PFA Players' Player of the Year prize in consecutive seasons in 2006-07 and 2007-08 during his time at Old Trafford.
Mohamed Salah, who won the award last year, was unable to retain it this time, while no Liverpool player was selected in the Premier League Team of the Year.
Arsenal and Manchester City dominate the Team of the Year
The composition of the PFA Premier League Team of the Year underlined just how heavily the 2025-26 campaign was shaped by Arsenal and Manchester City.
Fernandes was the lone Manchester United representative, while Brentford's Igor Thiago was the only other player from outside those two clubs.
Arsenal supplied five players to the XI, with goalkeeper David Raya joined by defenders William Saliba, Gabriel Magalhães and Jurriën Timber, while Declan Rice was selected in midfield.
Manchester City also had four representatives: Nico O'Reilly, Rayan Cherki, Antoine Semenyo and Erling Haaland.
The completed XI therefore contained:
- David Raya — Arsenal
- Jurriën Timber — Arsenal
- William Saliba — Arsenal
- Gabriel Magalhães — Arsenal
- Nico O'Reilly — Manchester City
- Bruno Fernandes — Manchester United
- Declan Rice — Arsenal
- Rayan Cherki — Manchester City
- Erling Haaland — Manchester City
- Antoine Semenyo — Manchester City
- Igor Thiago — Brentford
The PFA Team of the Year is effectively the players' all-star XI for the Premier League season, with professionals voting to select the best performers across the campaign.
For Fernandes, being included alongside such a dominant Arsenal and City contingent further emphasised the scale of his individual season.
O'Reilly beats Cherki to Young Player award
Manchester City's Nico O'Reilly had an equally memorable night after being named PFA Men's Young Player of the Year.
O'Reilly beat a shortlist that included his City team-mate Rayan Cherki, Arsenal teenager Max Dowman, Junior Kroupi, Manchester United's Kobbie Mainoo and Liverpool youngster Rio Ngumoha.
His campaign extended beyond club football, with O'Reilly also helping England finish with a bronze medal at the World Cup.
Reflecting on his season, O'Reilly said:
“I had a great season. I'm very proud of the season I had. I won two trophies with my club and managed to play at the World Cup with my country. I'm over the moon how it turned out.”
O'Reilly's award also complemented his inclusion in the senior PFA Team of the Year, making him one of the night's standout individual winners.
Bunny Shaw wins women's award for a second time
Manchester City's Bunny Shaw claimed the PFA Women's Players' Player of the Year for the second time.
Shaw had previously won the award in 2024 and now joins an exclusive group of players to have collected the women's prize twice.
Only Lucy Bronze, who won in 2014 and 2017, and Fran Kirby, who won in 2018 and 2021, had previously achieved that feat.
Shaw's latest victory followed another outstanding season in front of goal.
The Manchester City striker scored 21 goals in 22 Women's Super League appearances, winning the WSL Golden Boot and helping City claim their first top-flight title in 10 years.
Shaw was also selected in the PFA Women's Team of the Year.
PFA Awards 2026 at a glance:
Men's major awards

- PFA Young Player of the Year: Nico O'Reilly — Manchester City

stories.headline: We've developed winning culture, hungry for more, says Harmanpreet ahead of Asia Cup, Asian Games
stories.deck: Fresh from winning the first-ever women's Test match at Lord's by defeating England last month, India will now turn their attention to the UAE Asia Cup T20
stories.bodyText:
Indian women cricketers are "hungry for more" after a string of impressive victories, with captain Harmanpreet Kaur saying a winning culture is taking shape as they head into the Asia Cup in the UAE and Asian Games in Japan.
Fresh from winning the first-ever women's Test match at Lord's by defeating England last month, India will now turn their attention to the UAE Asia Cup T20, where they are record seven-time champions, before embarking on their title defence at the Asian Games in Japan.
"We of course expect to win. Our team has been playing very good cricket," the India skipper, who guided India to a historic Test win against England at the iconic Lord's recently, told Sony Sports.
"The last 4-5 years have been good, and where we have played good cricket, dominating cricket, have defeated big teams and won series also.”
The Kaur-led side had sealed a huge 270-run win over England at Lord's, marking India's second-highest win by margin of runs in Women's Tests, the fourth biggest overall.
"Now, we are coming after the win at Lord’s and have also won many games on the trot, so the team has already tasted success and will be hungry for more." In the upcoming Asia Cup, beginning Friday (August 28, 2026), India share Group A with arch-rivals Pakistan in the eight-team tournament.
After losing the last edition to Sri Lanka, India will look to reclaim the trophy, riding high on their recent Lord’s triumph.
"The best thing is, everybody in the team talks about how to win a match, how to win tournaments. So when you have that kind of culture, you always feel motivated and you and you really look forward to go for any tournament.”
"So this (Asia Cup) tournament is very important and I am sure we will play as a team and once again will make our country proud," said Kaur.
"I think the biggest challenge is when you have the ‘good team’ tag, playing for those expectations is in itself a very big challenge because we know we dominate Asian cricket and it’s very important to play every match with that domination," she opined.
On the hype surrounding India-Pakistan clashes, Kaur said the pressure is on another level, something players can genuinely feel despite being accustomed to high-intensity competitive cricket.
"No doubt it’s a high-pressure game and as a player you need to deal with multiple things. We keep playing international cricket but the amount of pressure in a India vs Pakistan match, that kind of pressure you don’t feel anywhere else.”
"Somewhere we know every Indian is watching, not only cricket fans but every Indian is watching because that match is so important for all of us.”
"As a captain and as a player, I try to keep things very simple, very easy. Only focus on cricket, focus on our aims, focus on our routines." Kaur said winning a gold medal for the country is a special honour for any cricketer, with the Asian Games offering a different feeling from ICC events as every player receives an individual medal.
India made their Asian Games debut in Hangzhou, winning gold, and will now chase another top finish.
"As a cricketer I think this is a very big opportunity because before this we have mostly played ICC tournaments but have not fought for a medal because as a team we have always fought for any particular trophy.”
"This is one such moment where you get your own medal and I think when it’s about the medals, the motivation increases even more. Day and night we keep thinking how will we feel after winning the medal and how we will celebrate.”
"It also gives the chance to witness other sports, meet other players, understand their routines so it’s not just only about cricket but knowing your other sports fellows also on how they prepare," added the gold-winning Indian skipper at Hangzhou.
Kaur acknowledged the weight of expectations at the Asian Games but said the team would remain focused on the task at hand, with preparations progressing in the right direction.
"Yes definitely, the last time we had played very dominating cricket and one-sided contests so there will be expectations from us to play that kind of cricket again.”
"I’m sure the country is looking forward that one gold medal coming from cricket, so I know pressure is going to be there, but at the same time, focusing on your job and how to achieve that job is more important."
Reflecting on India’s historic Lord’s win, Harmanpreet said: "Playing a Test match at Lord’s is a big dream for any cricketer. For me also, it was a very big dream and to lead the team is an even bigger dream."
"I think, before this, I had played just 4-5 Tests, but the feeling of playing at Lord’s was totally different. I think, till now, thinking about those four days we had lived, we are still talking about it."
