stories.headline: ‘Haaland leaving Man City is inevitable’: Ex-City star predicts exit timing
stories.deck: Former Manchester City midfielder Gareth Barry believes Erling Haaland could eventually leave the club if their dominance and trophy success decline. Despite his contract until 2034, Barry says Haaland may seek a new challenge if City struggle over the next two seasons. He also expects Arsenal to be favourites for the Premier League following City’s major changes.
stories.bodyText:
Erling Haaland's future at Manchester City may be secure for now, but one former City midfielder believes the Norwegian's long-term stay at the Etihad should not be taken for granted.
Haaland has committed himself to the club on a contract running until 2034 and remains the centrepiece of City's attack. Yet with the club entering a new era and facing questions over whether it can maintain the dominance of recent seasons, Gareth Barry believes the next couple of years could be decisive in determining whether the prolific striker eventually looks for a new challenge
Why Haaland could eventually look elsewhere
Haaland joined City in 2022 and has already established himself as one of the most prolific goalscorers in the club's history.
The 26-year-old has scored 162 goals in 200 appearances across all competitions for City, while playing a major role in a period that included a historic Treble in 2022-23. His long-term contract, signed in 2024, was designed to keep one of football's most coveted strikers at the Etihad well into the next decade.
But Barry does not believe the length of that agreement necessarily means Haaland will see it through.
Speaking exclusively to 
GOAL
, the former England international said: “Erling Haaland leaving Man City one day is inevitable.”
Barry stressed that Haaland has no reason to force an exit while City remain competitive, and expects the striker to avoid the kind of public agitation that has accompanied some high-profile transfers.
“As much as Haaland's association with City is really big, and that will keep him there for now, he won't be rocking the boat like you see a lot of other players doing,” Barry said.
Manchester City's Erling Haaland during the English Premier League soccer match between Manchester City and Bournemouth in Manchester, England, Sunday, Aug. 23, 2026. (AP Photo/Dave Thompson)
The former City player believes the situation could change if the club's trophy haul begins to decline.
“I think if City's dominance does wane a little bit and the trophies aren't coming in, it will fuel the speculation,” he explained. “It is natural sometimes to want a new challenge, and I'm sure Haaland will be no different.”
Barry's prediction is therefore less about Haaland wanting out immediately and more about what happens around him.
“It's not just going to happen overnight. Haaland will think about his career, which is short,” he said. “But if the trophies aren't coming in, it will just fuel speculation.”
And given Haaland's standing in the game, Barry expects the striker to have no shortage of options if he eventually decides the time is right.
“He will have offers from all over the world because he's the best striker in the world, so it's just natural. It's one you can see happening in the future.”
The next two years could be crucial
For Barry, the most important period may not be the end of Haaland's current contract but the next two seasons.
He believes the striker's eventual decision will be heavily influenced by how competitive City remain domestically and in Europe.
“A lot will depend on how competitive City are in Europe and the Premier League in the next year or two, I should imagine,” Barry said.
That is particularly significant given the changes taking place around Haaland.
Pep Guardiola has departed after his long spell in charge, while City are now entering a new era under Enzo Maresca. At the same time, Rodri has left, removing one of the most influential players from the team's midfield.
Those developments have led Barry to question whether City can immediately return to the top of the Premier League.
Barry expects Arsenal to be favourites
City have gone two seasons without winning the Premier League, with Liverpool and then Arsenal restoring themselves to the top of the domestic game.
Barry, who helped City win their first Premier League title in 2011-12, believes the latest changes could make a title challenge even more difficult.
“Even before selling Rodri, given the turnover of managers at City, it would have been tough to overturn Arsenal from where they are at the moment,” he told 
GOAL
.
“I think with Rodri going, they're even less of a threat now to challenge Arsenal.”
Barry expects City to strengthen further and believes new additions could ease the burden on Elliot Anderson and the rest of the midfield, but he does not think that will necessarily be enough to make them favourites.
“I'm sure they're going to sign one or two to improve and maybe replace him, which will help [Elliot] Anderson and the other players in that midfield,” he said. “I'd say they have less of a chance to challenge and maybe win the title now Rodri is gone. I won't say they've given the title away, but it’s making it a lot harder.”
His assessment of the title race is emphatic.
“I have Arsenal down as huge favourites,” Barry said. “I just feel with City, with what's going on, the threat is less and less this season and Rodri leaving has just added to that, really. So I can see the other clubs improving.”
He also expects Chelsea to progress after missing out on Champions League football, while believing Manchester United and Aston Villa could find European competition challenging.
Ultimately, Barry still expects City to finish second but sees a sizeable gap between them and Arsenal.
“I still think City will possibly be in second place, but they'll be less of a threat than they were last year,” he said.
Spain remains a possible destination
Haaland's future has already been linked with the two biggest clubs in Spain.
Real Madrid's long-standing pursuit of elite attacking talent means the Norwegian continues to be associated with a potential move to the Santiago Bernabéu, while Barcelona are also expected to consider options for the No. 9 position as they plan for life beyond Robert Lewandowski.
Those links have existed since Haaland established himself as one of Europe's premier strikers and could become increasingly prominent if City's competitive level drops.
A move to Madrid was even part of the platform of former Real Madrid presidential candidate Enrique Riquelme, who promised to sign Haaland had he won the club's election.
He did not, leaving the situation unchanged for now.
Manchester City's Erling Haaland shows his frustration during the English Premier League soccer match between Manchester City and Bournemouth in Manchester, Sunday Aug. 23, 2026. (Nick Potts/PA via AP)
There is no indication that Haaland is currently pushing to leave City, and his enormous contract gives the club significant security. But Barry's argument is that circumstances, rather than the contract itself, could ultimately determine the striker's next move.
If City continue challenging for major honours, there may be little reason for Haaland to look elsewhere. If that dominance begins to disappear, however, the equation changes.
For a striker who has already achieved extraordinary numbers at the Etihad and who is entering what should be the prime years of his career, the next two seasons could tell City, and Haaland, whether the future is still in Manchester.

stories.headline: KCL | Vathsal’s blistering knock steers Sailors home
stories.bodyText:
A statement knock (93, 53b, 11x4, 3x6) from captain Vathsal Govind eclipsed an unbeaten century from Mohammed Azharudden and powered Aries Kollam Sailors to a six-wicket win over Alleppey Ripples in the Kerala Cricket League at the Sports Hub Greenfield stadium on Tuesday.
Vathsal, who shed his image as an accumulator, rode his luck (dropped on zero and 67) to tear the Ripples attack to shreds and carry Sailors to their second win in the league.
Vathsal blended traditional shot-making with signature T20 shots like the ramp and reverse sweep to help Sailors chase down a target of 187 with 14 balls to spare.
Sailors started the chase disastrously, losing Arun Polouse for a duck, bowled through the gate by Vinil.
However, Abhishek J. Nair counterattacked and Vathsal, after the early reprieve, got into his groove, with the pair adding 96 runs for the second wicket in quick time.
Abhishek fell soon after completing his half-century, but Vathsal assumed the role of enforcer to take Sailors to the doorstep of victory. Earlier, Ripples overcame a slow start to post a competitive 186 for three, thanks to a late flourish from Azharuddeen (100, 51b, 6x4, 7x6).
Azharuddeen, who was dropped on 27, 29, 60 and 75, added 101 for the second wicket with Sachin Baby (40) and finished with a flourish by taking 19 runs from M.D. Nidheesh’s final over of the innings.
Enaan does it again!
Thrissur Titans moved to the top of the points table after scoring a thrilling one-wicket win over Trivandrum Royals. Titans needed 17 runs for a win after Sijomon Joseph’s three-wicket penultimate over tilted the match in favour of Royals.
However, for the second successive night, Mohammed Enaan (41 not out, 15b, 6x6) turned out to be a Titan as he smashed C.V. Vinod Kumar for three consecutive sixes to snatch an unlikely win.
The scores: Alleppey Ripples 186/3 in 20 overs (Mohammed Azharuddeen 100 n.o., Sachin Baby 40) lost to Aries Kollam Sailors 187/4 in 17.4 overs (Vathsal Govind 93, Abhishek J. Nair 52, K. Ajinas 2/45).
Trivandrum Royals 181/6 in 20 overs (Govind Dev Pai 76 n.o., Abhishek P. Nair 40, Krishna Prasad 30, Biju Narayanan 2/27) lost to Thrissur Titans 183/9 in 19.4 overs (Shoun Roger 68, Mohammed Enaan 41 n.o, A.K. Arjun 27, Sijomon Joseph 3/7).

briefs.headline: Ex-Man Utd star warns Neymar-Messi reunion could make MLS an even bigger circus
briefs.deck: Former Manchester United and Serie A forward Giuseppe Rossi has warned that Neymar joining Inter Miami would boost MLS commercially but do little to improve its footballing quality. While he supports a reunion with Lionel Messi and Luis Suarez, Rossi criticised MLS for prioritising superstar signings, clicks and club valuations over developing the league’s overall sporting standard.
briefs.bodyText:
Neymar
's potential move to Inter Miami has been framed as the perfect opportunity for another reunion with 
Lionel Messi
 and Luis Suarez, but one former Premier League and Serie A forward believes the move could expose a bigger problem within Major League Soccer.
Giuseppe Rossi, the former Manchester United and Villarreal forward who is now Head of Soccer at the New York Cosmos, has warned that bringing Neymar to MLS would be excellent entertainment and marketing, but would do little to improve the quality of football being played in the competition.
The Brazilian has been repeatedly linked with a move to Miami, where he could reunite with Messi and Suarez after their hugely successful spell together at Barcelona. For Rossi, however, the question is not whether supporters would want to watch it. It is whether another superstar reunion is actually helping MLS become a stronger football league.
Rossi questions what MLS is trying to become
Rossi made his comments while speaking to 
GOAL
 in an interview conducted in association with BetBrothers, and he was particularly critical of the league's continued reliance on globally famous players to generate attention.
MLS has undergone a major transformation through marquee arrivals over the years, with David Beckham, Steven Gerrard, Kaka, Andrea Pirlo, Zlatan Ibrahimovic and Wayne Rooney among the established stars who have moved to the United States.
Messi's arrival in 2023 took that strategy to another level, with the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner becoming the league's biggest attraction. Inter Miami subsequently surrounded him with several former Barcelona team-mates, including Suarez, Sergio Busquets and Jordi Alba, while Rodrigo De Paul and Casemiro have also joined the club.
Neymar could now become the latest superstar to make the move, with his Santos contract due to expire at the end of the year.
But Rossi believes MLS risks becoming too focused on the attention generated by those names.
“This is where MLS are making mistakes, and they continue to make these mistakes. It’s great marketing, it is what it is, but what kind of product are you putting on the field?” Rossi told 
GOAL
.
He specifically questioned the idea of bringing Neymar to Miami simply to recreate the famous Barcelona attack.
“Bringing Neymar back to reunite him with Lionel Messi and Luis Suarez, what are you trying to become as a league?”
‘You’re moving at a snail’s pace’
Rossi's concern is not that MLS has failed commercially. Quite the opposite.
He acknowledged the league's substantial growth and the increasing value of its clubs, but argued that the sporting product has not developed at the same rate.
“If it’s to get to the level of the big boys out in Europe like the Premier League, La Liga, Bundesliga and those competitions, you’re moving at a snail’s pace but MLS is very thirsty for clicks and views, and they don’t really care about the standard of the football itself,” he said.
Rossi went on to distinguish between the league's commercial success and its footballing development.
“Yes, they have made great strides, and well done to them for that. The valuations of the clubs are high and it’s a great business model but what about the football? Is that growing and moving forward? I don’t think so, and that’s something that has to change.”
He believes the underlying issue comes from the priorities of those running the competition.
“The problem is that the people in charge don’t really care. They only care about the valuations. That’s the problem when you put these billionaires in charge of a league.”
In Rossi's view, Neymar would therefore be an attractive commercial addition without necessarily addressing the competitive development he believes MLS needs.
“They’d love to see Neymar come to MLS and play with Messi again but it’s not going to grow MLS as a football league. That’s what I think.”
Rossi still believes Neymar could benefit from joining Messi and Suarez
Despite his criticism, Rossi was not arguing that Neymar is finished as a footballer.
Quite the opposite: he believes the Brazilian could still make a significant impact if he moved to Inter Miami and reunited with Messi and Suarez.
Neymar's World Cup story
Neymar, now 34, has endured a difficult period with injuries and inconsistent form since leaving European football, and his return to Santos has not produced the sustained revival many expected.
But Rossi remains convinced that the player retains the ability to make the move worthwhile on an individual level.
“If Neymar could make the move to Miami, why not? It would be great for him, and he’s still a great player. I freaking love Neymar,” Rossi told 
GOAL
.
He added that Neymar remains “one of the best players of his generation” and that supporters would naturally want to see him back alongside Messi and Suarez.
That is precisely where Rossi sees the contradiction: the reunion could be fantastic for the players, the supporters and the headlines, while simultaneously doing little to address what he sees as MLS's sporting shortcomings.
“I just look at it another way because there are pros and cons to everything, and yes everybody wants to see Neymar but it does take away from the integrity of the products itself by making MLS into even more of a circus than a true football league.”
The prospect of another MSN reunion
Neymar, Messi and Suarez previously formed one of the most devastating attacking partnerships in modern football at Barcelona.
Between 2013 and 2017, Neymar scored 105 goals and provided 76 assists in 186 appearances across all competitions for Barcelona, helping the club win eight trophies, including the 2014-15 treble.
The possibility of seeing the three together again, this time in MLS, would therefore carry enormous global appeal.
For Inter Miami, it would represent another blockbuster addition to a squad that has increasingly become a collection of some of the defining players of the modern era.
For MLS, though, Rossi believes the question should go beyond whether another superstar can generate clicks, ticket sales and commercial interest.
His warning is essentially about what happens after the spectacle: if the league wants to close the gap with Europe's strongest competitions, he believes improving the football itself has to matter just as much as attracting the biggest names.

briefs.headline: TNPL: Grand Cholas, Kovai Kings brace for battle of equals
briefs.bodyText:
Rain has been the most influential player of this TNPL playoffs. It washed out Qualifier 1. It returned for the Eliminator. And now, ahead of Wednesday’s Qualifier 2 at Chepauk, it has given Trichy Grand Cholas a rather useful advantage: if there is no result, it will join Madurai Panthers in the final.
That is because Grand Cholas finished second in the league, one place above Vida Kovai Kings.
If there is cricket, Kovai Kings will rely on a well-rounded bowling attack led by the tournament’s two most economical bowlers.
Left-arm spinner M. Siddharth has nine wickets while conceding just 5.33 an over, and leg-spinner Jhathavedh Subramanyan has 13 at 6.29.
Pacers K. Deeban Lingesh and G. Kishoor, with 12 and 10 wickets respectively, have provided further bite.
With the bat, B. Sachin, the tournament’s second-highest run-getter (377 at 167.55), will be crucial in the top-order.
If he provides the platform, skipper Shahrukh Khan — fresh from an unbeaten 18-ball 59 against Dindigul Dragons — and C. Andre Siddarth can accelerate.
Grand Cholas’ unconventional new-ball pair will pose a different challenge.
K. Easwaran, whose action was inspired by former Pakistan left-armer Sohail Tanvir, leads the wicket charts with 14 wickets, while the slinging Athisayaraj Davidson has taken 10.
With its top three of K. Rajkumar, J. Suresh Kumar, and S. Shyam Sundar forming the batting core, and Sanjay Yadav and R. Rajkumar providing the late flourish, Grand Cholas have the ammunition for another crack at the final, weather permitting.

briefs.headline: HIL’s third edition on shaky ground
briefs.bodyText:
Even as the Indian hockey teams returned disappointing performances from the ongoing World Cup, the revived Hockey India League’s third edition seems to be on shaky ground.
The HIL is battling for survival on several fronts barely two years after being re-launched with much fanfare. Multiple sources have confirmed to The Hindu that more than one existing team is on the verge of exiting and there are question marks over the women’s competition as well. In addition, very few foreign players have expressed interest in returning for the league.
“Last year, the Ranchi franchise came in as replacement for the Odisha team in the women’s competition and Gonasika among the men. Shrachi Tigers, who own the Bengal franchise among both men and women, are also on the lookout of investors to offload and exit,” federation sources admitted.
Earlier this year, owners of Ranchi Royals wrote to the HIL Governing Council seeking clarity on their continuation, non-receipt of promised sponsorship worth ₹10 cr. from the Jharkhand government and transparency in commercial terms. The franchise has since been terminated over non-payment issues with Hockey India clearing dues from the franchise’s share of revenue.
Among the four women’s team, only JSW Sports and APL Apollo, owners of Delhi SG Pipers, have agreed to continue in the league, albeit verbally at the moment, after considering an exit. Sources said talks are in final stages for a Bangalore-based team as well. “The women’s league will happen, and with four teams only. The modalities are still being worked out but there is no question of discontinuing it,” a source in the know insisted.
The men’s competition, however, is likely to see fewer teams down from the eight in the first two editions. “There may be a change of ownership or franchise city. The number of teams is also likely to be less, perhaps five or six at the most,” Hockey India officials said.
The league has been plagues with issues from the beginning. Gonasika was roped in as the eight men’s team on the day of Player Auction in 2024.
Ranchi’s original women’s team was accused of non-payment by several foreign players and even Shrachi managed to clear its dues for the 2025 season only towards the end of June. The lack of foreign players’ interest due to payment uncertainties also forced Hockey India to extend its initial registration deadline from July 24 to August 31.
It has also been reliably learnt that HI president Dilip Tirkey has had several rounds of meetings with franchise owners including Parth Jindal of JSW and Sanjay Gupta of APL Apollo, prospective sponsors and representatives of the Tata Group in the last one month across the country, trying to salvage the league.
It has also been learnt that the precarious situation around HIL and the series of meetings had led to Tirkey cancel his own travel for the World Cup and denying official permission to HI Director General Cdr. RK Srivastava, convenor the HIL Governing Committee, for the same, which was disregarded.

briefs.headline: Boxing selection twist: Kundu returns after Ministry intervention, Punia back in reserve
briefs.deck: Sumit Kundu retains his place in the Asian Games boxing team despite a recent loss in the trial match. Meanwhile, Deepak Punia, the victor of the trial, finds himself in a reserve position. The sports ministry's final decision to include Kundu raises concerns regarding the need for the trial altogether, significantly affecting both athletes amid the controversy.
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: In yet another bizarre twist to India’s Asian Games boxing selection, Sumit Kundu has retained his place in the men’s 70kg squad despite losing a fresh trial to 
Deepak Punia
, who has now been relegated to reserve.
The sports ministry’s final Indian contingent list has named Kundu in the 11-member boxing team — six men and five women — effectively overriding the outcome of the Boxing Federation of India’s (BFI) closed-door trials at NIS Patiala on August 17.
The development raises an obvious question: if Kundu was always going to remain the first-choice boxer, why was the fresh trial conducted in the first place?
The BFI had originally finalised its Glasgow CWG and Aichi-Nagoya Asiad squads following trials at NIS Patiala on May 13-15. The decision to reopen three categories — men’s 70kg and 90kg, and women’s 65kg — came after recommendations from the high-performance unit, support staff and selection committee.
Kundu, who had been originally selected, lost to reserve Punia in the 70kg bout and was replaced. The trial minutes stated that the winner would be Rank 1 for the Asiad, while the loser would remain reserve. However, they also carried a caveat that if the ministry and Indian Olympic Association (IOA) did not accept the revised entries, the boxers who had represented India at the CWG would retain their Asiad berths.
That is precisely what has happened. Kapil Pokhariya retained his 90kg place after beating Harsh Choudhary, while Parveen Hooda stayed in the women’s 65kg category after defeating Saneh.
BFI sources said the trials were necessitated to identify India’s best medal prospects after the trio failed to win medals at the CWG. Kundu lost 1-4 to Northern Ireland’s Jon McConnell in the pre-quarters in Glasgow.
But the process has left both Kundu and Punia paying the price. Sources said Sumit was around 75-76kg before the trial, making repeated weight cuts particularly demanding. After preparing for the CWG and August 17 trial, he must again cut weight for the Asiad, leaving his body completely drained.
It has been learnt that the boxing contingent is scheduled to leave India on September 4 for a pre-Games training camp in Japan before travelling directly to the Games.

briefs.headline: Duleep Trophy: Late wickets peg West back, leave contest wide open; East crushes North East
briefs.bodyText:
Some late-afternoon tardiness may end up costing West Zone its Duleep Trophy quarterfinal versus North Zone as it lost four wickets in the final 30 minutes of day three to close at 220 for seven, chasing 287.
This included set batters in Ruturaj Gaikwad (66, 70b, 7x4) and Musheer Khan (96, 126b, 8x4, 2x6), and it brought North back into a contest that had seemingly slipped from its grasp on an eventful Tuesday at the BCCI Centre of Excellence here.
Ruturaj risked a sharp single and was run out by a direct hit from wicketkeeper Kanhaiya Wadhawan while Musheer tried a wild one-handed sweep and was caught behind.
Until then, the duo had combined for an excellent 111-run stand for the fourth wicket. Ruturaj impressed with his wristy stroke-making and Musheer with his footwork. So much so that, the red-soil pitch, which had hissed and spluttered until then, turned a mute witness to their top-notch batting.
But their dismissals, followed by the twin setbacks in the final over off left-arm spinner Abid Mushtaq, left the match on a knife’s edge. There is some solace for West as Urvil Patel is still at the crease (17 batting, 17b, 3x4), and capable all-rounders in Shardul Thakur and Tanush Kotian are yet to bat.
Earlier in the morning, North Zone, from an overnight 107 for four, folded for 222, with Ayush Badoni top-scoring with 50 (62b, 6x4).
All 10 wickets were snared by spinners, with even Musheer claiming two.
The 21-year-old Mumbai cricketer will now hope that his all-round performance doesn’t go in vain.
On the adjacent ground, East Zone completed an innings and 210-run win over North East to set up a semifinal date with defending champion Central Zone.
North East was bundled out for 146 after having begun the day at seven for no loss. Anukul Roy took five wickets (five for 37), and 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi too joined the party (two for 11) with his handy left-arm spin.
The scores: North Zone 251 & 222 in 51 overs (Ayush Badoni 50, Nishant Sindhu 44, Shams Mulani 4/78, Tanush Kotian 4/46) vs. West Zone 187 & 220/7 in 51 overs (Musheer Khan 96, Ruturaj Gaikwad 66).
East Zone 467 bt North East Zone 111 & 146 in 50 overs (Anukul Roy 5/37).

briefs.headline: Kishan keen to regain place in Test squad
briefs.deck: The dashing stumper-batter says the competition is something else in the longest format; the 28-year-old adds he is happy for Jurel and Pant
briefs.bodyText:
In mid-2023, Ishan Kishan was an all-format player for India. With Rishabh Pant having suffered a horrific road accident, and K.S. Bharat not so impressive, Kishan made his Test debut in the West Indies that July and was also part of the limited-overs squads.
But since then, the dashing wicketkeeper-batter hasn’t played a red-ball game for India, and did not feature in a single white-ball international for two full years in 2024 and 2025.
It is only now, since the start of 2026, that he has regained his spot in T20Is and ODIs. A Test call-up is far, but the 28-year-old has his eyes set on making another comeback from the margins.
“I love this game,” Kishan said after leading East Zone to a thumping innings and 210-run victory over North East Zone in the Duleep Trophy quarterfinal on Tuesday. “I enjoy it because when you are in the middle, the ball is moving, players are coming at you, and there is banter.
“It’s easier to bat on flat tracks and it’s fun as well, but competition in Tests is something different. People don’t believe me when I say that, but I really do enjoy red-ball cricket.”
But being a regular in the white-ball set-up means he barely gets any time to turn out in whites. Prior to this outing, his last First Class match was more than nine months ago. It is highly likely that the Duleep Trophy will be his only brush with the long format until early 2027.
“That is the fun part actually,” Kishan insisted. “You need to put a lot of effort to get back in the Test team. Dhruv [Jurel] is doing so well; Rishabh [Pant] is doing so well.
“But I am very happy for them, [despite] being a competitor. My job is to not think about what can go wrong for them. My job is to just keep getting better”.

briefs.headline: Emotional meeting for Savita and Bichu with late coach’s wife
briefs.bodyText:
India’s two goalkeepers, Savita Punia and Bichu Devi, were set to go through their training drills, ahead of their crucial World Cup match against Australia on Sunday, when a poignant moment unfolded by the advertising boards.
They were approached by Caroline Busch, wife of the late Simon Zijp, a renowned goalkeeping coach in Dutch hockey. Zijp, who had been training Savita and Bichu since the start of last year, was set to return to India last November before his untimely demise in October.
Caroline had travelled from Hague and wanted to take this opportunity to reconnect with the girls, due to the strong bond they shared with Zijp. She handed them some chocolates, a couple of small wooden shoes — a symbol of Netherlands’ farming history — and a personal note.
“In the note, I wrote that Simon always talked very highly of them. I also wished them a lot of luck and success for the future,” said Caroline while wiping away her tears.
For Savita, the unexpected meeting with Caroline turned into a pleasant memory.
Savita said Zijp’s words through her rehabilitation process during her injury spell allowed her to come back stronger.
“He used to talk to me about what is important for a senior player to come back after an injury. And if there is an injury, how many thoughts come to the mind? He used to ask me to write down those thoughts in a diary to keep motivating myself,” said the veteran ’keeper.
According to Savita, the whole team was shocked to hear of his death. “I also realised that we all developed so much attachment over such a short time so I wondered how tough it would be for the family,” said Savita.
She had previously spoken to Pirmin Blaak, the current goalkeeping coach of the side, about how special their former coach was for her.
Zijp was a long-time coach of Blaak, the former Netherlands goalkeeper. So Blaak promised that he would arrange for a meeting with Caroline, which he fulfilled.
Savita was grateful for that opportunity, which allowed her to make one final connection to her former coach through his wife. “She took time out to come meet us, despite it being a very tough time for her. She [Caroline] gave us good wishes and blessings, it will be a lifelong memory for us,” added Savita.

briefs.headline: Asian Games tennis row deepens as AITA rebuts SAI's omission allegation
briefs.deck: The All India Tennis Association (AITA) has rejected claims it failed to submit the names of excluded Asian Games tennis players to the IOA, with TimesofIndia.com accessing a July 3 letter seeking their inclusion. AITA argued event-specific selections would maximise medal prospects, but the Sports Ministry has stood by its strict Asia-ranking criteria despite criticism from ex-player Rohan…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: The row over India's tennis squad for the 2026 Asian Games intensified on Tuesday after the All India Tennis Association (AITA) categorically rejected claims that it failed to submit the names of excluded players to the Indian Olympic Association (IOA).
The national federation denied a claim made by Sports Authority of India (SAI) source to news agency PTI that the omitted players — Manas Dhamne, Sahaja Yamalapalli, Vaishnavi Adkar, Vaidehee Chaudhari and Prarthana Thombare — did not feature in the shortlist forwarded by AITA to the IOA, and therefore were absent from the final list considered by the Sports Ministry.
However, 
TimesofIndia.com
 has accessed the letter dated July 3 which was sent to the IOA CEO Raghuram Iyer where merits of each player, including recent history, was mentioned.
AITA stated that Secretary General Sunder Iyer had written to Iyer on July 3, making an "urgent representation seeking review of the exclusion of tennis players from the Indian contingent" and specifically naming Dhamne, Ankita Raina, Yamalapalli, Chaudhari, Adkar and Thombare.
In the four-page letter sent on July 3, accessed by 
TimesofIndia.com
, AITA had argued that India should field its strongest possible contingent and maximise medal opportunities across all five tennis events rather than relying solely on uniform ranking criteria.
On Monday, as 
TimesofIndia.com
 reported, the Sports Ministry had stuck by its selection policy, which requires singles players to be among Asia's top six and doubles players to be inside the continental top-eight over a 12-month evaluation period. The ministry has also maintained that the criteria will not be relaxed despite criticism made by two-time Asian Games medallist 
Rohan Bopanna
.
AITA's case for the quartet
The federation's representation highlighted that India had earned multiple strong acceptance-list positions in doubles events.
AITA said India had three mixed doubles pairs inside the top-eight accepted entries — Rutuja Bhosale/Yuki Bhambri (seeded No. 2), Ankita Raina/N. Sriram Balaji (No. 5) and Prarthana Thombare/Anirudh Chandrasekar (No. 8). Since each country can enter only two pairs, AITA argued this represented two genuine medal opportunities.
It also pointed out that Thombare and Bhosale were positioned at No. 10 on the women's doubles acceptance list, with withdrawals potentially opening the door to the main draw. Excluding established doubles specialists, the federation said, would weaken India's medal prospects.
For the singles events, AITA described Yamalapalli as India's highest-ranked women's singles player, praised Adkar's international multi-sport credentials, backed Chaudhari's consistency on tour and termed 18-year-old Dhamne one of India's brightest young prospects whose Asian Games participation would aid both immediate competitiveness and long-term Olympic development.
The letter concluded by requesting the IOA to urgently review the exclusions, reassess entries on an event-specific basis and approve all six players to maximise India's medal chances.
Ministry steadfast in exclusions
The controversy erupted after the exclusion of five players from the original 12 member list drew criticism from two-time Asian Games gold medallist Rohan Bopanna.
Bopanna had said that "a committee that never stood where they stood has decided their fate on paper, before a ball is struck," adding that denying players the chance to compete was against the principles of building a sporting nation.
The Ministry, however, has maintained that recent performances did not establish sufficient medal probability and argued that creating discretionary exceptions for players ranked between 25th and 40th in Asia would undermine administrative integrity and invite litigation from other national sports federations.
India's final tennis squad currently includes Sumit Nagal in men's singles, while Yuki Bhambri, Dhakshineswar Suresh, N. Sriram Balaji, Anirudh Chandrasekar, Ankita Raina and Rutuja Bhosale have been selected for the doubles events.
